item.text:
Continuing the audit, I added controls to the malformed-input battery and precisely localized the defect class. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_08-06-10-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

**Extended battery (7 cases now, `audit/malformed_rpc_battery.log`):**

```
installSnapshot/badConfiguration    -> PANIC   (F1)
installSnapshot/badPeers            -> handled without panic
appendEntries/unknownLogType        -> PANIC   (F2)
appendEntries/badConfigurationEntry -> PANIC   (F3)
appendEntries/deprecatedPeerBadData -> handled without panic
requestVote/garbageCandidate        -> handled without panic
requestPreVote/garbageCandidate     -> handled without panic
```

The four non-panicking cases are deliberate controls, and they matter: the *analogous* peer-input paths (`decodePeers` for the legacy `Peers` field and deprecated peer-set entries, plus the vote request/grant handlers) all reject bad bytes by returning an error or ignoring them. That precisely localizes the defect to exactly three call sites where peer bytes reach `DecodeConfiguration` (two) or `prepareLog`'s `default` `panic` (one) — it is not a vague "the RPC layer is fragile" claim. I recorded this narrowing in §3.4.

I also reviewed the FSM batching loop (`fsm.go`: `applySingle`/`applyBatch`/`restore`/`snapshot`) for ordering or response-corruption bugs; it is standard and correct, and its only untrusted-input hazard is the same `DecodeConfiguration` path already covered (F3 shadows it).

**Status:** the audit's concrete output remains F1/F2/F3 (one localized class of RPC-reachable, unauthenticated, remote-crash defects, inherited from upstream v1.7.3, tree still byte-identical to the release), plus negative/benign evidence for everything else. Everything reproduces with `bash audit/run_all.sh`; `go vet` and `go build` are clean; the intentionally-crashing end-to-end case stays env-guarded.

Remaining gaps unchanged: the ~15 TCP/loopback test groups need the private-loopback `isolated_exec` (nested `bwrap` denied here), and `fuzzy/`/`raft-compat/` have no offline reference or runnable dependencies.
